newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firm on T-bill demand, reserves payments.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firm on T-bill demand, reserves payments.

text.p: The rouble firmed on Thursday as banks sought funds for monthly compulsory reserves and demand for government securities, dealers said.
Dealers noted the rouble, strictly ruled by Russia's central bank, was not affected by President Boris Yeltsin's annual state of the nation speech, delivered to Russia's parliament today.
Roubles/dollar Mar 6 midday Mar 6 early Mar 5 close
"Rouble demand has been high these last two days as the dealine for setting aside reserves is tomorrow," one dealer said.
Neftekhimbank dealer Boris Golub said some funds could also be going to the Treasury bill market after Wednesday's auctions yielded more than the secondary trading level.
On March 5 the central bank auctioned 7.5 trillion roubles of six-month paper and an additional tranche of 4.5 trillion roubles of six-month bills.
